notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical inference across flight ops and MRO workflows. Primary ask = deterministic latency SLOs + reserved capacity plan for mixed throughput patterns.

Workload profile: short chat-like safety alerts (avg 40 tokens, p99 target 50-60ms), reranking of maintenance transcripts (batch jobs at night, throughput spikes ~800 req/s for 10-15m), embeddings for similarity search (dense index updates overnight).

Model preference: prefer open Llama-family 70B variants for quality; willing to consider quantized 4-bit profiles for cost if latency/SLOs preserved. Also test a trimmed 13B fallback for critical low-latency paths.
Quantization/compilation notes: ask from infra team — need recommendations on 4-bit vs 8-bit quant profiles per context length; want kernel-level latency benchmarks for context lengths 512/2048/8192.

KV cache & batching: want guidance on continuous KV-cache sizing and batching policy to meet p99 targets during bursts without >2x token-cost increase. Interested in hybrid: small-batch fast-path + large-batch cost-path for low-priority reranks.

SLA ask: 99.9% availability, p99 latency SLO per route (separate SLOs for safety-alert vs analytics). Procurement pushing for explicit SLA credit schedule and defined fallback model behavior if SLOs missed.
Quote from CTO (Anya Patel): "If an alert path exceeds 100ms p99 we cannot certify onboard workflows. Need deterministic guarantees or clear degraded-mode plan."

Security: must run in customer VPC for flight-data PII, KMS integration mandatory, retention controls + audit logging per audit team. Also asking about on-prem air-gap feasibility for limited instances (future phase).

POC plan: 2-week dedicated-capacity POC: baseline (stock model, no quant) -> quantized profile A/B -> batching/KV cache tuning -> failover to 13B fallback. Deliverables: latency/throughput matrix, recommended reserved GPU counts, cost delta estimates.

Deal velocity: medium. Legal and security teams engaged; procurement wants SLA table before moving to commitment. AE note: emphasize Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce unit cost during non-peak windows.
